documents.text: The Halden orchard grows forty varieties of apple. Harvest begins in the second week of September and lasts five weeks. Pickers are paid by the crate, and each crate holds eighteen kilograms. The cider press was installed in 1987 and still runs on its original motor.

The island ferry sails six times a day in summer and twice a day in winter. A single crossing takes forty minutes. Bicycles travel free, but cars must be booked a day ahead. The service is suspended when wind speed exceeds fifty knots.

Members may borrow up to twelve items for three weeks. Overdue fines were abolished in 2021. The reading room on the top floor is silent, while the ground floor allows conversation. Rare maps can be viewed by appointment only.

Stoneware is fired to 1240 degrees Celsius over eleven hours. The kiln must cool for a full day before it is opened. Glazes containing copper turn green in an oxidising atmosphere and red in a reducing one. Shelves are coated with a wash so that drips do not fuse to them.

The city marathon starts at seven in the morning at the old harbour. Water stations are placed every five kilometres. Runners who have not reached the thirty kilometre mark within four hours are asked to board the sweep bus. The course record is two hours and nine minutes.

A healthy hive holds around fifty thousand bees in midsummer. The queen can lay two thousand eggs a day. Honey is taken in late August, leaving at least twenty kilograms for the colony to survive the cold months. Smoke calms the bees by masking their alarm scent.
